item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Lord Blackwood, GENTLEMAN ADVENTURER in a most curious expedition through space. This is awesome. I will admit I had not read either of the two SCPs involved in this story before, so I was pleasantly surprised throughout this tale.

It also reminded me a bit of H.G. Wells' First Men In the Moon. Which is a good thing.

I love the Blackwood stories, and while I admit they don't have the same feeling they had when I was reading the Tarasque hunt, the quality of your writing offsets anything they might have lost. Yes, the stories are not new anymore, but they are very solidly written, entertaining pieces that are a refreshing look at the Foundation verse. Keep doing what you're doing.

Speaking of you doing what you're doing, how on Earth are you getting them out so fast Smapti? Admit it, you're really a group of a thousand genetically engineered monkeys wired up to a thousand internet connections writing the greatest work in the English language, right?

item.content:encoded:
Don't be preposterous.1 Blackwood has only interacted with SCPs which existed in the nineteenth/early twentieth century (or could plausibly have done so). Iris is much too young. Similarly, he could never have encountered Smokey, the Rocket Surgeon, the Radio Raccoons, the Autonomous SWAT Armor, or the Meteorological Dog.

Ironskin, Ariel, Freiherr von Schwarzwald, Herr Chirurg, the Scripted Nightclub, or the "peculiar unwashed man with some odd accent that sounded Polack", however…

Footnotes
1. and I use the word in the sense of its original etymology!
